summary: This episode discusses how the Prophet ﷺ, back from the Isra' and Mi'raj without protector or Khadijah, looked for a new base for da'wah by meeting the tribes who came to the markets and encampments of the Hajj season. The ustaz reads authentic and weak narrations of the Prophet ﷺ offering himself, helped by Abu Bakr, an expert in Arab genealogy, being stoned and followed by Abu Lahab who called him a liar, and being rejected by tribes such as Banu Kalb, Banu Hanifah and Banu Amir, who asked for a guarantee of power. He also tells of individuals who later accepted Islam such as Suwaid, Iyas, Dimad and Tufayl, and the six Khazraj youths at Aqabah who opened the way to Madinah. The lessons are the courage to be disliked, the art of negotiating without selling out principle, not giving up on anyone, and our responsibility to convey Islam, starting with those closest to us.
keyPoints: After the Isra' and Mi'raj the Prophet ﷺ returned to Quraysh propaganda without Khadijah, Abu Talib or Mut'im's protection, and stepped up his meetings with tribes from outside Mecca during Hajj.
The Prophet ﷺ offered himself directly to the tribes and asked whether anyone would take him into their people so he could convey his Lord's word, and this went on for ten years.
Abu Bakr, an expert in Arab genealogy, prepared a profile of each tribe, its strengths and allies, so the Prophet ﷺ could use a different approach for each group.
Abu Lahab followed the Prophet around the market calling him a liar, and the Prophet did not answer him.
Banu Amir asked for a guarantee of leadership after the Prophet, and he refused to sell out his principles, replying that the matter belongs to Allah.
Many individuals such as Suwaid, Iyas, Dimad and Tufayl accepted Islam after brief meetings, including after listening for themselves despite being warned not to.
Six Khazraj youths who lived beside the Jews heard the Prophet at Aqabah and became the beginning of the Hijra to Madinah.

chapters.title: Introduction and the supplication when praised
chapters.summary: The ustaz reviews the last episode on the courage to be disliked and Abu Bakr, and the supplication when praised mentioned in Al-Adab Al-Mufrad and Hisnul Muslim.

chapters.title: The Prophet ﷺ without a protector
chapters.summary: Mut'im withdrew support, Abu Talib and Khadijah were gone, and Abu Lahab withdrew his protection.

chapters.title: Back from the Isra' and thinking strategically
chapters.summary: The Prophet ﷺ returned to Mecca with the wisdom of the heavens but was still anxious, and stepped up his efforts to meet the tribes.

chapters.title: Markets and the Hajj season
chapters.summary: Hajj was shopping season, with markets like Ukaz, Majannah and Dhul Majaz where tribes from afar gathered.

chapters.title: Calling every day and being rejected
chapters.summary: The Prophet ﷺ called people every day to say la ilaha illallah, was spat on and had dust thrown on him, then comforted his daughter.

chapters.title: The pressure in Surah Al-Kahf
chapters.summary: The background to Surah Al-Kahf and the verse that he might destroy himself with grief over their rejection.

chapters.title: The Quraysh campaign and self-doubt
chapters.summary: The Quraysh campaign made tribes see bad reviews, and the ustaz links it to self-doubt when long effort brings no result.

chapters.title: Hadith of Jabir: offering himself
chapters.summary: The sahih hadith of Jabir that the Prophet ﷺ offered himself to people in the Hajj season, and ten years of open calling.

chapters.title: Abu Bakr and different approaches
chapters.summary: Abu Bakr and Ali accompanied the Prophet; Abu Bakr prepared tribal profiles and acted as first spokesman.

chapters.title: Pointed at and followed by Abu Lahab
chapters.summary: Tribes pointed at the Prophet with their fingers, and narrations of Rabiah and Tariq say Abu Lahab followed and stoned him.

chapters.title: Banu Kalb and Banu Hanifah
chapters.summary: The Prophet praised the name of Banu Abdullah's father, and the story of Thumamah, chief of Banu Hanifah, who later accepted Islam.

chapters.title: Banu Amir and the guarantee of power
chapters.summary: Banu Amir asked for a guarantee of leadership and the Prophet refused to sell out principle; an old man among them regretted the refusal.

chapters.title: Individuals who accepted: Suwaid and Iyas
chapters.summary: Suwaid, called Al-Kamil, and Iyas, still a child, listened to the Prophet, then were killed in Madinah as believers.

chapters.title: Dimad and Tufayl
chapters.summary: Dimad wanted to treat the Prophet with incantation but accepted Islam, and Tufayl, who stuffed his ears with cotton, finally heard and believed.

chapters.title: Six Khazraj youths at Aqabah
chapters.summary: Six youths who lived beside the Jews heard the Prophet and responded, including As'ad ibn Zurarah.

chapters.title: Closing: the work of da'wah and courage
chapters.summary: The Prophet asked Al-Abbas for help, and the ustaz stresses that da'wah is not just for religious people, and the courage to be disliked.

people.role: Protector of the Prophet from the Quraysh
people.context: Gave protection after Ta'if but turned negative after the Prophet told of the night journey.
Withdrew his protection, followed the Prophet around the market and called him a liar; the Prophet did not answer him.
An expert in Arab genealogy who prepared tribal profiles, acted as first spokesman, and taught the supplication when praised.
Tied up in the mosque for three days, saw how Muslims lived, and accepted Islam without direct da'wah.
Wanted to accept the Prophet in order to rule the Arabs and asked for a guarantee of leadership after him.
A leading poet who heard the Quran from the Prophet and accepted Islam, then was killed in Madinah.
Still a child when he heard the Prophet and said it was better than what they had come for; died a Muslim.
Meant to treat the Prophet, said to be mad, heard the khutbat al-hajah three times, then accepted Islam.
Stuffed his ears with cotton so as not to hear the Prophet but eventually listened and accepted Islam.
One of the six at Aqabah, aged nineteen, who would later begin Friday prayer in Madinah.
A businessman with a wide network who had not yet accepted Islam but did not obstruct.
Mentioned as an example of the Companions' expertise; the Prophet told him to learn Quraysh genealogy from Abu Bakr.

lessons.title: Be brave in calling our friends
lessons.body: Many of us have good friends we have never spoken to about Islam for fear of rejection, yet the Prophet ﷺ tried again and again, gently.

lessons.title: Be careful when praised
lessons.body: The Companions including Abu Bakr taught a supplication so we are not drunk on praise, asking Allah to make us better than people think.

lessons.title: The courage to be disliked
lessons.body: The Prophet ﷺ chose to keep conveying even though it was unpopular, mocked and rejected every day.

lessons.title: Don't rush to conclusions about failure
lessons.body: Someone who fails repeatedly easily thinks it is not for him, but the Prophet kept going, and we do not know that one small conversation can change someone.

lessons.title: Adapt the approach to the audience
lessons.body: Abu Bakr prepared a profile of each tribe so the Prophet ﷺ used different approaches, not one way for all.

lessons.title: The art of negotiating without selling out principle
lessons.body: The Prophet did not flatly refuse but stressed that leadership is in Allah's hand when asked for a guarantee of power.

lessons.title: Don't give up on anyone
lessons.body: We do not know that one small conversation can change someone, and he may return ten years later with his whole village.

lessons.title: Hear it from the person himself, not about him
lessons.body: Algorithms close our ears to different views; Tufayl stuffed his ears but finally listened and believed, so listen yourself before rejecting.

lessons.title: Start with genuine curiosity
lessons.body: The Prophet listened to Suwaid's recitation first before offering something better; sincere curiosity opens the door of the heart.

lessons.title: Da'wah is not just for religious people
lessons.body: The Companions were merchants, commanders, farmers and students who brought religion alive in all their roles.

lessons.title: The obstacle is the way forward
lessons.body: Calling the closest family is the hardest, but without facing it we remain passive.

glossary.meaning: The big Hajj-season markets where goods and tribes from across the Arabian Peninsula gathered.
An Arab clan or people; its members usually could not change allegiance except in rare circumstances.
A post that deliberately provokes anger so people share and comment; the ustaz links it to the Quraysh campaign that made people curious.
The title of Suwaid ibn Samit for his poetic brilliance and noble lineage.
An area in Mina where the Prophet met the six Khazraj youths.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions a supplication recorded in Al-Adab Al-Mufrad, listed in Hisnul Muslim as the 232nd, and linked to Abu Bakr. The third part appears in Al-Bayhaqi's narration.
dalil.translation: O Allah, do not hold us to account for what they say, forgive me for what they do not know, and make me better than they think.

dalil.context: The ustaz says some sirah scholars weaken this narration, but it shows the Prophet's daily perseverance.
dalil.translation: Mudrik narrated that the Prophet ﷺ called out, O people, say la ilaha illallah and you will succeed; some spat, threw dust and insulted him until midday, then a girl brought water and he said do not fear that your father will be defeated or humiliated.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions the background of Surah Al-Kahf in the Jews' questions and the instruction not to say one will do something without insha'Allah. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: do not say of anything, ‘I will do that tomorrow,’

dalil.context: The ustaz reads the verse that the Prophet might destroy himself with grief if they do not believe. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: But [Prophet] are you going to worry yourself to death over them if they do not believe in this message?

dalil.context: The ustaz compares it to the people of Prophet Nuh who put their fingers in their ears. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: every time I call them, so that You may forgive them, they thrust their fingers into their ears, cover their heads with their garments, persist in their rejection, and grow more insolent and arrogant.

dalil.context: Allah knows the Prophet's chest tightened from thinking about those who did not listen. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: We are well aware that your heart is weighed down by what they say.

dalil.context: The ustaz says this narration is sahih and explains that a tribe could not change allegiance except in rare cases.
dalil.translation: Jabir RA narrated that the Prophet ﷺ offered himself at the Hajj gathering place, asking whether anyone would take him into his people because the Quraysh were preventing him from conveying his Lord's word.

dalil.context: The ustaz says it is also a narration of Jabir and shows ten years of open da'wah up to Khadijah's death.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ sought out the Hajj pilgrims at their lodgings for ten years.

dalil.context: The ustaz says this narration is sahih according to hadith scholars.
dalil.translation: Rabiah ibn Ibad and Tariq ibn Abdillah saw the Prophet ﷺ in the Dhul Majaz market calling people to say la ilaha illallah, while a man behind accused him of lying and stoned him until both heels bled; that man was Abu Lahab.

dalil.context: The ustaz says the purpose of different peoples and tribes is to know one another, and links it to listening to others' perspectives. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: People, We created you all from a single man and a single woman, and made you into races and tribes so that you should recognize one another. In God’s eyes, the most honoured of you are the ones most mindful of Him: God is all knowing, all aware.

dalil.context: The ustaz says this narration is very weak, but shows the Prophet asking for help from Al-Abbas's network.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ told Al-Abbas that he saw no protection with him or his brother, and asked Al-Abbas to take him to the market to show where the tribes were.

sirah.era: After the Isra' and Mi'raj and before the Hijra, in Mecca and Mina
sirah.summary: This episode tells of the Prophet ﷺ seeking a new base for da'wah through the Hajj-season tribes, with repeated rejection, a few individuals who believed, and the meeting with six Khazraj youths at Aqabah.
